notes: Captured on joe 2026-09-18 with Tools/capture-disc.sh v2: scan, lsdvd, the five IFO tables, 16 menu stills and their OCR. menus/structure.json from that run was DISCARDED, not committed: the helper's NAV reader had a four-byte error in the PCI structure (pci_gi is 60 bytes, not 64) and reported zero buttons for all 29 menu PGCs of a disc that carries 151 NAV packs full of them. The reader is fixed and now publishes its own self-checks, but no structure.json from this disc has been read with the fixed version yet, so `menus.structure` is false and every tier-1 expectation below is null. Re-capture to fill them in; DiscCorpusTests will then assert the headline invariant (play button target == outcomeIndex == 1) with no new test code. Stills are not committed: copyrighted menu artwork, and docs/menu-intelligence.md 8.7 leaves that to the user; menus/ocr.json carries everything the invariants read. REVIEWED 2026-09-18: expect.menu checked page by page against the 16 stills. audioTrackCount and subtitleGroupCount are still unfilled and are skipped rather than asserted.

menu.notes: Two things the archive recorded rather than smoothed over. (1) The subtitle list is what the app's own MenuOCR.Settings read, not what the page prints: the page prints English / Francais / Japanese / Off, and Vision reads three of the four whichever way it is configured — with the 1.3 language list it reads the Japanese and drops 'Off', with its defaults it reads 'off' and drops the Japanese. (2) Chapter 6 is recorded as 'No man's land.i'. The trailing '.i' is the decorative glyph after the caption; the first capture's still rendered it such that OCR read '*', which clean() strips, and this capture's still rendered it as 'i', which it does not. That is a wrong name at the right timestamp — the cheap failure of 3.3 — and adding a cleaning rule on one disc's worth of evidence would be the expensive kind. It is also direct evidence that which frame the still comes from matters, which is 1.2's open question. The same re-render read the title card correctly as 'Bloodsport' where the first read 'Bloodiport'.
